poem.author: 李峤
englishLines: It can shake down autumn leaves,
And open flowers in early spring.
Crossing the river, it raises towering waves,
Entering bamboo, it bends ten thousand stems.

appreciation.zh: 诗里没有直接画出风，却让我们从落叶、春花、江浪和竹林看见它。看不见的风，走到不同地方就留下不同的动作。
appreciation.en: The poem never shows the wind itself. We see it through falling leaves, opening flowers, river waves, and bending bamboo—an invisible visitor leaving movement everywhere.

pages.zhText:
解落三秋叶，
能开二月花。
过江千尺浪，
入竹万竿斜。
pages.enText:
It can shake down autumn leaves,
And open flowers in early spring.
Crossing the river, it raises towering waves,
Entering bamboo, it bends ten thousand stems.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Whimsical four-season Tang landscape connected by flowing ink-wash wind currents: autumn leaves, early spring blossoms, broad river waves and green bamboo bending, a curious Tang child in pale ochre robe follows the breeze, no literal wind character, no text.

pages.zhText:
解落三秋叶，
秋风从树梢跑过，金黄和红色的叶子纷纷飘落。
pages.enText:
It can shake down autumn leaves.
Autumn wind races through the treetops and sends gold and red leaves drifting down.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Same child in autumn grove, safe gentle gust lifts many gold and red leaves in spirals from trees, child holds hat and laughs, no storm, no text.

pages.zhText:
能开二月花。
早春的风变得轻柔，吹醒枝头一朵朵小花。
pages.enText:
And open flowers in early spring.
The softer spring breeze wakes small blossoms along the branches.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Same child in early-spring orchard, breeze moves across bare twigs as pale pink buds and blossoms open naturally, warm new light and tender green, no magic wand or text.

pages.zhText:
过江千尺浪，
风越过宽阔的江面，平静的水立刻卷起一层层浪花。
pages.enText:
Crossing the river, it raises towering waves.
When wind crosses the broad river, the water rises into rolling waves.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Same child watches from a high safe riverbank as strong wind creates dramatic but non-dangerous layered blue-green waves across a broad river, no boats or people in water, no text.

pages.zhText:
入竹万竿斜。
风钻进竹林，成千上万根竹子一起弯下腰，又轻轻弹起。
pages.enText:
Entering bamboo, it bends ten thousand stems.
Wind enters the grove; countless bamboo stems bow and spring back.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Same child at edge of dense green bamboo grove, thousands of slender stems lean together in one direction under wind then rebound, child safe on open path, no broken bamboo, no text.

pages.zhText: 风没有颜色，也没有形状。可是树叶、花朵、江水和竹子，都替它画出了走过的路。
pages.enText: Wind has no color or shape, but leaves, flowers, water, and bamboo draw the path it travels.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Poetic continuous panorama connecting leaf spiral, blossom petals, river ripples and bamboo sway into one visible path around same child, natural movement only, no literal creature, no text.

pages.zhText: 同一阵风，有时轻柔，有时有力。闭上眼睛时，你会从哪里发现它来了？
pages.enText: The same wind can be gentle or strong. With your eyes closed, how would you know it has arrived?
pages.illustrationPrompt: Quiet sensory portrait of same child closing eyes in meadow, hair ribbon, sleeves, grasses and one feather show a light breeze, calm curious mood, no text.

pages.zhText:
解落三秋叶，
能开二月花。
过江千尺浪，
入竹万竿斜。
再轻轻读一遍吧。
pages.enText:
It can shake down autumn leaves,
And open flowers in early spring.
Crossing the river, it raises towering waves,
Entering bamboo, it bends ten thousand stems.
Now read it softly once more.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Closing wide landscape with same child walking home as gentle wind trails through leaves, flowers, river and bamboo in balanced sequence, calm golden light, no text.
